title: Legislative districts of Maguindanao

{{Short description|Legislative districts in the Philippines}} {{Use Philippine English|date=March 2023}} {{Use mdy dates|date=March 2023}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Maguindanao''' were the representations of the [[Provinces of the Philippines|province]] of [[Maguindanao]] and the [[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|independent component city]] of [[Cotabato City|Cotabato]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The province and the city were represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through their [[#1st District|first]] and [[#2nd District|second]] congressional districts from 1987–2022. == History == {{further|Legislative district of Mindanao and Sulu|Legislative district of Cotabato}} Prior to gaining separate representation, areas now under the jurisdiction of Maguindanao were represented under the [[Department of Mindanao and Sulu]] (1917–1935) and [[Cotabato]] (1935–1972). The enactment of Presidential Decree No. 341 on November 22, 1973, created the Province of [[Maguindanao]] out of [[Cotabato]]'s [[Maguindanao people|Maguindanao-majority]] municipalities.{{cite web|title=Presidential Decree No. 341 - Creating the Provinces of North Cotabato, Maguindanao and Sultan Kudarat |url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1973/11/22/presidential-decree-no-341-s-1973/ |website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines |last=Marcos |first=Ferdinand E. |access-date=November 19, 2017 |date=November 22, 1973}} The new province was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region XII]] from 1978 to 1984. Maguindanao (including [[Cotabato City]]) first gained separate representation in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]], when it returned [[#At-Large (defunct)|two representatives, elected at large]], to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]]. Under the new Constitution which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987, the province, including [[Cotabato City]], was reapportioned into two congressional districts;{{cite web|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|website=Official Gazette of the Republic of the Philippines|url=http://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|date=February 2, 1987|access-date=November 19, 2017}} each elected its member to the restored [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|House of Representatives]] starting [[1987 Philippine legislative election|that same year]]. The province of [[Shariff Kabunsuan]], established with the passage of Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 201{{cite web|title=Muslim Mindanao Autonomy Act No. 201 - An Act Creating the Province of Shariff Kabunsuan, Providing Funds Therefor, and for Other Purposes|url=http://rla-armmgov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/MMAA-201.pdf|author=Regional Legislative Assembly - Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao|date=September 7, 2006|access-date=November 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170225122706/http://rla-armmgov.ph/wp-content/uploads/2015/03/MMAA-201.pdf|archive-date=February 25, 2017|url-status=dead}} and its subsequent [[2006 Shariff Kabunsuan creation plebiscite|approval by plebiscite]], was created out of Maguindanao's western municipalities in 2006. Per Section 5 of MMA Act No. 201, [[Cotabato City]] was grouped with Shariff Kabunsuan for the purpose of electing a congressional representative. It was this specific provision that became the subject of the [[Sema v. COMELEC and Dilangalen|Supreme Court case]] that ultimately voided MMA Act No. 201 for being unconstitutional, and leading to the disestablishment of the Shariff Kabunsuan in 2008 and the return of its territory to [[Maguindanao]]. In the brief period of [[Shariff Kabunsuan]]'s existence the [[#1st District|First District of Maguindanao—Cotabato City]] was known as the ''Lone District of Shariff Kabunsuan—Cotabato City'', while the [[#2nd District|Second District]] was known as the ''Lone District of Maguindanao''. The districts were dissolved in 2022 following the [[2022 Maguindanao division plebiscite|division]] of Maguindanao and replaced by [[Maguindanao del Norte's at-large congressional district]] and [[Maguindanao del Sur's at-large congressional district]] == 1st District (defunct) == *'''[[Cities of the Philippines|City]]''': [[Cotabato City]]{{efn|group=1|[[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|Independent from the province]] and does not vote for provincial officials.
